title: Swim in Rising Water
summary: Water rises one unit per second over a grid of distinct heights. When can you first swim from one corner to the other?

tests.explain: Going down then right visits heights 0, 2 and 1, so it is usable once the water reaches 2. Going right first needs the 3 to be covered. The answer is 2.
Down the left column and along the bottom row visits 0, 1, 2, 3, 4: at time 4 the whole route is under water.
The start cell has height 3, so you can't leave it before time 3. By then the route 3 → 1 → 2 is covered.

hints: You can stand on a cell once the water level reaches its height. A route is usable at time t exactly when every cell on it has height at most t.

So the answer is the smallest possible 'highest cell' over all routes from (0, 0) to (n - 1, n - 1). That is a minimax path, and Dijkstra handles it: the cost of extending a route is max(time, grid[nr][nc]).
Push [grid[0][0], 0, 0] into a min-heap, always expand the lowest time, and return the time when you pop the bottom-right cell.

complexity.time: O(n² log n): n² cells, each pushed a few times, with logarithmic heap operations
complexity.space: O(n²): the best-time grid and the heap
